items.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996
items.q: Well you’ve been with some of the great big bands, from Gerald Wilson through Benny Carter.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. I have enough trouble with the single reeds.
They’re nasty, oh my. Well you’ve been with some of the great big bands, from Gerald Wilson through Benny Carter. Tell me how the Thad Jones-Mel Lewis band kind of gelled into a great organization.

Gee. I knew Thad, I had met him in San Francisco when he was with Count Basie, and we played together at an after hours place there. And I met Mel through playing with Peggy Lee in New York and then eventually with Benny Goodman. We went to Russia and Mel was the drummer with Benny Goodman. And I knew both of these guys separately. I didn’t know them together. And then Mel called one day and said, “Oh, Thad Jones and I are starting a band and we would like you to play in the band.
